candidates.label: includesObject
candidates.comment: A composition relation between an offer or product collection and the specific products and their quantities it contains. Also called composed of, contains, comprises, consists of, has as object. Examples: An offer includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 2 apples. A product collection includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 5 books. A demand includesObject a TypeAndQuantityNode for 1 car.

candidates.label: hasBioChemEntityPart
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation between a biochemical entity and one of its constituent biochemical entities. Also called composed of, contains, includes part, made of. Examples: "A protein has a BioChemEntity part of an amino acid sequence.", "A cell has BioChemEntity parts like organelles.", "A molecule has BioChemEntity parts of atoms."

candidates.label: geoContains
candidates.comment: A geo contains relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place fully encloses another, with at least one interior point in common. Also called: encloses, encompasses, includes. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo contains "City 'Paris'", "Continent 'Europe'" geo contains "Country 'Germany'", "Building 'Empire State'" geo contains "Office 'Suite 100'". Distinct from geoWithin, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: members
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: includes members, comprises, consists of. Examples: "Club Organization members John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership members Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization members Partner Company". Distinct from member, which is a singular form and essentially the same concept.

candidates.label: comprisedOf
candidates.comment: A compositional relation between an anatomical system and the anatomical structures or other systems that physically comprise it. Also called "composed of", "consists of", "includes". Examples: "Circulatory system comprisedOf Heart", "Digestive system comprisedOf Stomach".

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: hasDefinedTerm
candidates.comment: A term inclusion relation between a defined term set or taxon and one of its contained defined terms. Also called contains term, includes term, term within. Examples: "A medical glossary has a defined term for 'hypertension'.", "A taxonomy has a defined term for 'Homo sapiens'.", "The dictionary has a defined term for 'algorithm'."

candidates.label: isPartOfBioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical part-whole relation indicating that one biochemical entity is a component of another larger biochemical entity. Also called component of biochem entity, contained within biochem entity, element of biochem entity. Examples: A protein domain isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a larger protein'. A subunit isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a protein complex'. A specific gene sequence isPartOfBioChemEntity 'a chromosome'.

candidates.label: includedComposition
candidates.comment: A composition inclusion relation between a music composition and a smaller music composition that is part of it. Also called part of composition, contains composition, movement of. Examples: "A symphony has an included composition as a movement.", "A musical work includes a composition.", "This composition contains several included compositions.". Distinct from hasPart, which is a general part-whole relation for creative works.

candidates.label: deathPlace

Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". candidates.label: spatial

Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". candidates.label: event

Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. candidates.label: sportsEvent

Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". candidates.label: contentLocation

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode

candidates.label: subjectOf

candidates.label: worksFor

candidates.label: owns

candidates.label: isRelatedTo

Distinct from isSimilarTo, which implies functional similarity, and isAccessoryOrSparePartFor or isConsumableFor, which imply specific functional dependencies. This is a very general relation.

candidates.label: employee

Distinct from member, which indicates a general affiliation rather than an employment relationship.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: isPartOf

Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: observationDate
candidates.comment: The date or date and time when an observation was made. Also called date of observation, observation timestamp, recorded date. Examples: "Weather Observation observationDate '2023-10-27'", "Medical Observation observationDate '2023-10-26T14:30:00'", "Astronomical Observation observationDate '2023-09-15'". Distinct from observationPeriod, which is the duration of the observation.

candidates.label: byDay

candidates.label: byMonthDay

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: applicableCountry
candidates.comment: An applicable country relation between a merchant return policy and the country where it is valid. Also called valid in country, country of application, policy region. Examples: "A return policy's applicable country is 'US'.", "The merchant return policy applies to 'Germany'."

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin
candidates.comment: A provenance relation between a creative work or product and its country of origin. Also called: origin country, produced in, made in. Examples: "French Wine" country of origin "France", "Japanese Anime" country of origin "Japan", "German Car" country of origin "Germany", "Hollywood Movie" country of origin "United States". Distinct from countryOfAssembly, which specifies where the product was put together.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: candidate
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a vote action, indicating the person who is being voted for. Also called "voted for", "nominee", "electoral candidate". Examples: "Election vote action candidate Jane Smith", "Award vote action candidate John Doe".

candidates.label: certificationStatus
candidates.comment: A status relation for a certification, indicating whether it is active or inactive. Also called "certificate status", "certification validity", "status of certification". Examples: "Product certification certificationStatus Active", "Company certification certificationStatus Inactive".

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

relations.definition: Indicates that an entity opposes or resists something.
relations.embedding_query_text: takes_stand_against: Indicates that an entity opposes or resists something.

chosen_property.label: opposes
chosen_property.definition: Indicates that an entity opposes or resists a concept or thing.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property expresses opposition; minted.

candidates.label: antagonist
candidates.comment: An antagonist relation between a muscle and another muscle whose action opposes it. Also called opposing muscle, counteracting muscle. Examples: "The biceps' antagonist is the 'triceps'.", "The quadriceps' antagonist is the 'hamstrings'."

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: endorsers
candidates.comment: An endorsers relation between a diet and the people or organizations that support or recommend it. Also called "supporters", "advocates", "recommenders". Examples: "Diet 'Mediterranean Diet' endorsers 'World Health Organization'", "Diet 'Vegan Diet' endorsers 'PETA'", "Diet 'Keto Diet' endorsers 'Dr. X'". Distinct from endorsee, which is the entity being supported.

candidates.label: hasRepresentation
candidates.comment: A representation relation between a biochemical entity and its common symbolic or structural representation. Also called represented by, symbolic form, structural representation. Examples: "A BioChemEntity has a representation as a chemical structure.", "The entity has a representation as a text sequence.", "This biochemical entity has a URL representation."

candidates.label: acceptsReservations
candidates.comment: A reservation acceptance status indicating whether a food establishment allows bookings. Also called takes reservations, booking available, reservation policy. Examples: "A restaurant accepts reservations is true.", "The cafe accepts reservations via its website URL.", "This diner accepts reservations is 'No'."

candidates.label: contraindication
candidates.comment: A medical restriction relation for a medical device or therapy, indicating a contraindication. Also called "medical warning", "precaution", "not recommended for". Examples: "Drug therapy contraindication 'Pregnancy'", "Medical device contraindication 'Pacemaker users'".

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: worksFor
candidates.comment: An employment relation between a person and an organization, indicating the organization for which the person is employed. Also called employed by, affiliated with, works at, employed at. Examples: Employee worksFor CompanyA, Consultant worksFor AgencyB, Professor worksFor UniversityC. Distinct from memberOf, which indicates general membership in a group, not necessarily employment.
